title: The archived infrared fits of Gaia20cdd give weak evidence for carbon and permit silicate dust below 0.3 au
abstract: We test whether the warm excess of Gaia20cdd selects carbon dust at a few au. We reconstruct the amplitude profile for all 18 published grain cases at 60 radii from two verified SCI files. All 1,080 original joint objectives agree within 2.85e-14. Under the original errors and constant emission, the minimum chi-square is 14.288 for silicate and 12.817 for graphite. The maximum likelihood ratio is 2.09. Radii within four objective units of the global minimum span 0.089-0.289 au for silicate and 1.540-5.539 au for graphite. A factor-of-two bound on the change in dust cross-section between 2010 WISE and 2025-2026 SPHEREx reduces the ratio to 1.21. Reducing the W3 error from 0.95 to 0.01 at its current flux raises the ratio only to 2.30 on this grid. The warm excess does not select a unique material or radius in the tested cases. The failure of a fixed hot-silicate solution does not exclude silicates at another radius. This is a finite-grid reanalysis with diagonal errors, not new photometry, a variability measurement, or a joint optical and infrared fit. We provide code, input hashes, aggregate profiles and a retrieval script.

display.caption: Material and epoch assumptions change the dust radius profiles. The W3 sensitivity test gives a small carbon preference at the archived flux. Objective contours are descriptive, not calibrated confidence sets.

citations.reason: We use its archived infrared fits and spectra. We quantify the weak material preference and the effect of an epoch-change bound.
Its grain cases enter the source emission grid. We test the radius and composition inference from that grid.
Original SPHEREx ice and excess report; the ice identification is outside our test.
Corrects the first-author name of Mittal et al. (2015). Numerical results are unchanged.
